data.narrative:
Climeworks, a Series F climate technology company, operates within a competitive frontier-energy landscape populated by one public comparable (Linacre, ticker LNZA) and eight private peers including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix. The company has raised over $1.0B to date.

Valuation analysis relies primarily on stage-progression methodology, as a sufficiently narrow peer set at identical or adjacent stages with comparable valuation tiers does not exist within the Climate & Energy sector. Applying a 1.3x step-up multiplier—typical for Series F advancement—to the $1.0B total-raised proxy yields an implied valuation of $1.3B. This method captures progression risk and dilution patterns observed across similar-stage financings but is constrained by limited transaction visibility in this emerging sector.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $1.1B (low) to $1.5B (high), with a median of $1.3B. The width of this range reflects reliance on a single applicable method and the structural scarcity of closely comparable transactions. Key uncertainties include path-to-profitability visibility, regulatory support durability, and capital intensity of scaling direct air capture technology. A more precise valuation would benefit from expanded comparable transaction data or detailed unit economics disclosure.
